title: RAW UNREVIEWED: one named plant has flower dye and unripe-fruit rind leather uses
summary: Pliny Natural History 13.34 explicitly owns one pomegranate entry: its named flower balaustium serves dyeing, while the skin of the unripe fruit serves leather dressing. This source-owned organ-to-use split is different from a flower/fruit season sequence or a generic reproductive-part list. Freeze the complete source paragraph, plant identity, organ, maturity state, and use before any Voynich comparison. A candidate full reading of an already admitted nonreserved owner would have to bind a flower term and a fruit-rind term independently, then preserve their unequal uses under both chor/shor assignments. This source does not identify any Voynich plant or word; no target is nominated or test selected. A botanical image alone or one matching dye word cannot orient the pair.

design.mechanism: One named plant partitions its flower and unripe fruit rind into distinct, source-written practical uses
design.unit: Pliny Natural History 13.34 complete pomegranate paragraph and only a later independently owned admitted manuscript entry
design.contrast: chor=flower/shor=fruit versus the reverse, with a generic two-organ list as a third rival
design.prediction: A fixed complete reading must associate the independently bound flower with dyeing and the independently bound unripe fruit rind with leather dressing; the reverse swaps their source-owned uses and a generic list lacks the two use relations. If neither organ or use has an independent target binding, all readings remain open.
